text:
matt: just finished the fleet fw rollforward ~10m ago, getting a weird spike in provisioning failures in eu-west-3. ~12% of GPU nodes failing at provision step. oob logs show secure_boot_policy flipped to 1 after flash on a subset of boards. anyone else seeing secureboot toggles?

infra-oncall: seeing the same. provisioner jobs stuck at 'attest' -> node stays NotReady. Kube reports kernel-args mismatch. Escalating to firmware owners.

ben: which fw/image did we push? exact build id pls.

matt: image: fw-2024-04-24-19:12, BMC bundle bumped v2.7.4 -> v2.8.0. snippet from oob daemon: ```Apr 24 19:17:03 oobd[1278]: flash complete: image=fw-2024-04-24-19:12, secure_boot_policy=1```

carmen: that build included the secureboot watchdog toggle patch to enforce lockdown on new hw. it should be opt-in — looks like a mis-flag in the build manifest triggered it for some boards.

ryan: note eu-west-3 spare GPU capacity is low today (bkds at 82% util). if we rollback we'll need to shift workloads -> higher egress/latency and cost. what's the blast radius?

matt: preliminary: affected hosts are mixed; majority are racks r04-r08. looks correlated with vendor X MCU revision. logs show nvram writes on those hosts: ```nvram_write_fail: rc=0x17 addr=0x1f```. 5–10% show nvram failures which might need manual intervention.

infra-oncall: recommend canary rollback of fw -> v2.7.4 for 100 nodes first. I'll open the rollback run.

deploy-bot: deploy:start rollback fw v2.7.4 scope=eu-west-3 canary=100 initiated by infra-oncall

ben: also seeing IPMI entries where secure boot bit is toggled by BMC during reboot sequence: ```IPMI: set_secure_boot: old=0 new=1 source=watchdog```. sounds like the watchdog agent is applying a policy on first-boot.

carmen: quick mitigation: we've pushed a config patch to oob-daemon to disable the auto-watchdog toggle for vendor X boards. patch id cfg-2024-04-24-02. applying to canary hosts now.

matt: temporary provisioner workaround: we can skip attest for jobs that match image=fw-2024-04-24-19:12 and vendor=X by setting PROVISION_SKIP_ATTEST=true. risky but helps reclaim capacity. anyone object?

ben: fine for canary. capture audit log. add guard so it only applies to jobs with tag "fw-canary-20240424".

ryan: SRE: we might need to enable burst capacity in us-central for 24–48h. cost estimate ~+$4.2k/day if we spill 200 GPUs. Approve if rollout takes >45m.

infra-oncall: canary rollback progress: 100 started, 95 succeeded and rejoined cluster, 5 failed with nvram_write_fail and require serial console intervention. marking those to manual queue.

matt: good news. can we hold off full region rollback until we confirm the config patch prevents toggles? we should also blacklist the problematic MCU batch.

carmen: agree. we're building a filter in the provisioner to detect vendor X MCU rev < 3 and force fallback image v2.7.4. also adding a post-flash verify step to read secure_boot flag and auto-fix via ipmitool when safe.

infra-oncall: quick command we used for the manual fix on canary (DO NOT run broadly): ```ipmitool raw 0x30 0x45 0x00``` — flips secure boot off for tested boards. we ran it only via serial with human in loop. risk: mis-run can leave board in inconsistent state.

ben: collecting serial logs for the 5 failed nodes and opening vendor ticket. ticket #VND-8732. include nvram dumps and board fw-id.

ryan: I'll trigger temporary burst and tag finance. if this stretches beyond today we'll need exec sign-off.

matt: prepping runbook for full rollback if canary proves clean. planned ops window in 1h. runbook snippet: "1) pause new provisioning 2) trigger canary rollback complete 3) patch provisioner rules 4) monitor join-rate and GPU allocation 5) migrate active jobs if capacity < threshold"

infra-oncall: monitoring dashboards updated, alerting when provision success rate drops below 90% or when gpu-ready count decreases by >50. sending AS nyc channel summary. :white_check_mark:

carmen: patch cfg-2024-04-24-02 applied to canary, will promote to region if no regressions in 30m.

matt: thanks all — keep updates here. we'll do another status post in 20m. :thumbsup:
